back_translation: O LORD, remember what has come upon us. Look and see our disgrace!
Our inheritance has been handed over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
We have become orphans without a father; our mothers are like widows.
The water we drink we must buy with money; our firewood comes only at a price.
We are pursued hard at our necks; we are exhausted and given no rest.
We stretched out our hands in submission to Egypt and to Assyria, to get enough food.
Our ancestors sinned and are gone, but we must bear the punishment of their iniquities.
Slaves now rule over us; there is no one to free us from their hands.
We risk our lives to get our food, because of the sword in the wilderness.
Our skin is hot as an oven from the fever of hunger.
The women have been violated in Zion, the virgins in the towns of Judah.
Princes have been hung up by the enemies' hands; the elders are shown no respect.
Young men must carry millstones; boys stumble under heavy loads of wood.
The elders are gone from the city gate; the young men have ceased their music.
Gladness has gone from our hearts; our dancing has turned into mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
Because of this our hearts are faint; because of these things our eyes grow dim.
Because of Mount Zion, which lies desolate, with foxes prowling over it.
You, O LORD, reign forever; Your throne endures through every generation.
Why do You forget us forever? Why do You forsake us for so very long?
O LORD, bring us back to Yourself, and we will return. Renew our days as in days of old —
unless You have utterly rejected us and are angry with us beyond measure.
